children.value: > Fact From Story Epic also claims that Google is illegally tying its Google Play payments platform to the Google Play app store, keeping other potential app payment mechanisms from competing as well.

> > Fact From Story Epic argues that Google makes it so difficult for developers and users to get around its Android app store, and that app store’s standard fees, that it’s created an illegal monopoly that unjustly enriches Google while artificially driving up app prices because other stores can’t compete.
> > > Fact From Story Google requires apps to use its own first-party billing system, and charges app developers a 15% to 30% commission on the sales it processes.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Tying products together can limit consumer choice.
> > Fact From Story Epic wants to break up Google’s alleged monopoly on Android app stores and payment methods, so developers aren’t stuck paying the “Google Tax” or passing that fee along to you.

> > > Fact From Story Epic argues that Google makes it so difficult for developers and users to get around its Android app store, and that app store’s standard fees, that it’s created an illegal monopoly that unjustly enriches Google while artificially driving up app prices because other stores can’t compete.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Artificially driving up app prices disadvantages consumers.
> > Commonsense Knowledge A company that controls the payment platform for its app store can dictate terms and fees.
> Commonsense Knowledge A monopoly restricts competition and can lead to increased prices.
